**Run EvalPerf against our local endpoint** — lowest friction in the cluster: Apache-2.0, native `--backend openai --base-url`, ~15 min/model, ~100 MB. It emits shared-qid coverage, McNemar/accuracy deltas, BSV signature severity, blockers, JSON/Markdown, and nonzero exit on a blocked candidate. Follow-up `5b29eead` adds `eval-result-pair`, so the same report can compare standalone paired-run EvalResult-like JSON artifacts without needing journal ingestion first. Orchestrator `939750c7` adds `scripts/autopilot/bsv_paired_runner.py`: a default-safe plan-only CLI that, with explicit `--run`, applies baseline/candidate params sequentially, evaluates the same core, writes baseline/candidate EvalResult JSON artifacts, restores baseline params by default, and emits the existing BSV paired report. Follow-up `a3570d8d` restores baseline params even when candidate application fails before candidate eval. Orchestrator `2bdb7abc` wires the mutation accept path behind default-off `AUTOPILOT_BSV2_ACCEPT_GATE`: prompt, GEPA, and code mutations run a pre-mutation baseline eval only when the flag is on, compare baseline/candidate EvalResult vectors through the paired-report backend, reject/revert on `gate_decision=block` or blocking signature severity, accept+annotate watch/pass cases, and preserve existing single-eval behavior when the flag is off. Remaining work is operator-approved live paired runs / rollout evidence before enabling the flag in production windows.

Conflict severity increases on shared subsystem/file/section/flag overlap, blocking BSV deltas, different behavior surfaces, or disjoint/opposing sentinel movement across accepted mutations. **A11 — E5 DOES have absence-inferred fields; census done ✅ 2026-08-11 (`mainA`).** Answering the rider at `handoffs/active/autopilot-sequential-allocation.md` (`f272bb4e`), which measured the era label being inferred from a MISSING question ledger on ~61% of 1372 autopilot journal rows and asked whether E5 has the analogue. **It does — three, and I introduced two of them tonight.** Write-up: `/mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/e5-a6-trimmed-window/A11-absence-inferred-fields-in-E5.md`. The shape is not "a field is missing" (that is ordinary) but **absence READ AS A VALUE** — unfalsifiable from the record, because a row that never had the field and a row whose true value equals the default are byte-identical. Measured: `reasoning` present on **19/191** manifests (all gemma4, and 10 gemma4 still lack it); `binary_version` present on 3 of 7 cpu_bench rows; `generated_at` absent on the whole legacy corpus. Benign by contrast: `decision_grade_blockers` 33/128 and 28 measurement fields at 110/128, where every reader guards with `or []` or an explicit branch.

**The `binary_version` discriminator was mine and had the defect — FIXED ✅ 2026-08-11, research `ecb99de8`.** Block A deliberately chose presence-of-`binary_version` as the kernel-cutover discriminator over an added `boundary_kind`. That cannot distinguish `E8-cpu-bench-throttle-scope` (genuinely not a cutover, correctly excluded) from `E5-cpu-kernel` (**a cutover whose binary nobody recorded**, excluded for the wrong reason). Harmless today; not harmless once an `E10-cpu-kernel` row is appended without the field, since it would read as "not a cutover" and derivation would keep returning `E9` — the silent staleness this repair exists to remove, reintroduced by its own fix. A row that NAMES itself a cutover and carries no binary now raises, naming the row, when it is the row that would have answered the query. Scoped not to over-fire: an older unwitnessed cutover superseded by a witnessed one stays silent, or `E5` would break every present-day query. Tests 65 → 66; 191/191 still valid.

**`reasoning` — write side CLOSED ✅ 2026-08-11 overnight, research `567ffa16`.** The 2026-07-29 fix amended 19 gemma4 *artifacts* and never the generator: `make_cell` recorded no `reasoning` for any model, so **regenerating the grid would silently have reverted it** — measured, a freshly generated gemma4 cell lacked the field while its banked equivalent carried it. Every model now states its mode (`gemma4` `off`; the other three `auto`, recording today's behaviour rather than changing it), `make_cell` always emits it, and the **result row now records the effective mode beside `sampling`** so a banked row can finally answer "reasoning on or off?" without resolving a manifest path that may since have been regenerated. The launched command is deliberately byte-identical — `auto` still omits the flag, since `--reasoning auto` *should* equal omitting it and should-be is not verified-to-be in a zero-cells lane; pinned by a test. Sweep suite 64 → 65; 191/191 banked manifests still valid.

**Residual, needs a run (not this lane): backfill the 172 banked manifests that lack `reasoning`.** Absence means the flag is not emitted (`server_numa_np_sweep.py:464`), so the server runs `--reasoning auto`, which for `arch=gemma4` is **ON** — the opposite of what both registries record. Already measured: 41/43 capture failures on the W2 smoke and the same signature behind W0's 430/430 (`5d6a17f2`). **The 10 gemma4 manifests lacking the field are exactly the 10 divergent pairs** in the duplicated-W0 row above — one defect seen from two directions. Two asks: (a) persist the effective `reasoning` into each result row beside `sampling`, so a banked row can say which mode produced it; (b) backfill `reasoning` explicitly onto the 172 manifests that lack it, including `"auto"` where that is intended. Not done here — proving (a) end to end needs a run, which is outside this lane's zero-cells boundary.

**`generated_at` absence-inference is MINE, bounded, and deliberately kept.** The validator reads its absence as "legacy manifest, validate loosely". Every alternative measured worse — design doc 01 §4 found git last-touch would reject 19 of 191 real files and mtime is worse. It is defensible only because it has a **closing horizon**: it can apply solely to manifests written before today and shrinks as the corpus regenerates. Residual worth closing cheaply: a *future* manifest that loses the field takes the loose path silently. Guard = require `generated_at` once `schema_version` is at or past the version introducing it; deferred because bumping `e5-cell-manifest/1` is a schema change with its own consumers.

**The executed `reasoning` mode is not recorded in ANY result row (filed 2026-08-11 `mainA`; unowned, small, no trust boundary).** `reasoning` is read from the manifest solely to build the server command (`server_numa_np_sweep.py:460`) and never written into `cells.jsonl` — verified the key is **absent**, not null, in the banked W2 gemma rows. So a banked row cannot answer *"was this measured with reasoning on or off?"*; the only route is to follow `manifest.json → args.cell_manifest/manifest_dir` back to a file on disk, which is exactly what breaks once a manifest directory is regenerated — i.e. the row above. **Same defect class as the A7 era mis-stamp, one field over: the run manifest records the CLAIM but not the WITNESS.** For a setting that already produced a 41/43 capture failure and a 430/430 W0 wipeout, that is thin. Fix: persist the effective `reasoning` into each row beside `sampling`, which is already recorded exactly this way and for exactly this reason. Not done in this lane — it is outside the zero-cells offline-replay boundary, since proving it end-to-end needs a run.

**FOURTH stale era constant — a LIVE TOOL OUTAGE, fixed ✅ 2026-08-11 (`mainA`), research `bcfcd0a5`** — `epyc-inference-research/scripts/benchmark/cpu_prefill_v8_regression_runner.py:480` pinned the same `{E6-cpu-kernel, E7-eval-instrument}` pair, but unlike the other three it fails **CLOSED**: it asserts `scoped[-1].get("id") == expected_id` and raises `registry active <scope> row drifted`. Verified by execution against the live registry — it raises on **both** scopes, so the v8 prefill regression runner **could not start at all**, and had not been able to since the v8 cutover of 2026-07-25. Nobody hit it because nobody invoked it. Its docstring says it binds to the **active** eras, so this was accidental staleness, not a deliberate historical pin. **Not repinned** — a constant there goes stale at every cutover by construction, which v9 proved a second time. Now derives the active row from the append-only registry (last row of a scope = newest), deliberately positional rather than date-derived *because of the scope collision noted above*. Still fails closed on a missing file, an empty scope, a row with no id or no `from`, and a mid-hash registry change. Verified binding: `cpu_bench` → `E9-cpu-kernel`, `eval_quality` → `E16-eval-history-scoped-quiescence-v10-quality`. **The old drift test REQUIRED the outage** — it appended a newer era and asserted the attestation raised — so it was replaced, not adjusted; a guard whose green state is the defect cannot survive the fix. Added a literal-scan test that no era id is a string literal in the runner, verified to fail against the pre-fix source (which hardcodes two).

**THIRD stale era constant, AutoPilot fail-safe (routed to `inference`, not mine to touch)** ✅ **2026-08-11 — CLOSED by `mainA` at operator instruction, orchestrator `190ccab4`.** Its value is untouched (E7 was a real boundary; a deliberate past pin is legitimate) — what changed is that nothing treats it as *current*: the registry-unreadable fallback now reads `active_instrument_eras.eval_quality` **and** `quality_exclude_before_ts` from `autopilot_state.json`, a witness the era-advance path maintains. The old fallback under-fenced by three weeks. The test asserting the stale behaviour was REPLACED, not adjusted. — `epyc-orchestrator/src/autopilot_core/instrument_era_guard.py:26` `E7_EVAL_INSTRUMENT_ERA_ID = "E7-eval-instrument"`, stale since `eval_quality` moved to E8 on 2026-07-25. Its own comment says the constant **MUST** match the registry row it stands in for, and it is the **fail-safe fallback used when the registry read fails** — so on registry failure AutoPilot fails **open to a stale era**. `tests/unit/test_instrument_era_guard_eval_quality.py:46` asserts it equals the stale literal, so **the test pins the staleness**. Same fixture-masking pattern as the dead detector. All three lines verified directly.

**Era ids are not derivable by pattern — three traps, one rule (2026-07-29, verified)** ✅ **2026-08-11 — the rule is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not just recorded** (`mainA`, research `9ed5fcb4`/`ecb99de8`): `scripts/lib/instrument_era.py` derives every era and no era id is a string literal in the generator — pinned by a literal-scan test verified to fail against the pre-fix source. Trap (a) ordinals-vs-versions is now unreachable because nothing reads an ordinal; the `-cpu-kernel` suffix is used only to DETECT a contradiction (a cutover with no `binary_version`), never to order eras. — recorded here because all three bit real work today and the same rule defeats all three.

**W2 focused post-fix capture smoke — PASSED ✅ 2026-07-29** (`e5-w2-capture-smoke-20260729T183019Z`, verdict exit 0, `decision_grade=true`, `dry_run=false`). Decisive before/after inversion once `--reasoning off` reached the server (research `5d6a17f2`): **empty answer text 41/43 → 0/43**; **rows carrying `reasoning_text` 43/43 → 0/43** (no reasoning channel emitted at all); **offline-scorer `parse_ok` 0/43 → 43/43**; `capture_fail_close_cells` 0; `failures: NONE`. This closes the W2 precondition **and confirms the re-attribution**: the capture contract was always sound and its fail-close fired truthfully — reasoning-mode-ON was what consumed the 256-token budget. Note property 3 (the offline scorer sees scoreable answer text) is now genuinely **exercised**, which the pre-fix run never reached. The decision-grade Gemma W2 sweep started automatically behind the gate at 18:31:51Z. Original text below.

~~W2 focused post-fix capture smoke~~ (superseded by the PASSED entry above) — before the decision-grade Gemma W2 sweep, run a focused generated-answer capture check using the hardened SSE contract: persist `reasoning_text` separately, require nonempty answer-text deltas when tokens were generated, and prove the offline scorer sees scoreable answer text — **and confirm the launch line actually carries `--reasoning off`**, which is what PREVENTS the failure; the smoke only DETECTS it (re-attributed 2026-07-29, research `5d6a17f2`: the budget sink was reasoning-mode-ON, not the capture parser). The historic W0 Gemma `430/430` parse failures have no raw SSE ledger and cannot be recovered. **Precondition on the operator artifact**: this smoke must pass BEFORE any decision-grade W2 run; the published results artifact's W2 section (see below) must stop describing the Gemma group as quality-invalid only once real quality data exists from this smoke.

**W2 smoke STAGED + verdict tooling landed (zero inference)** ✅ 2026-07-29 (research `c48bcb60`) — `scripts/benchmark/e5_w2_capture_smoke_check.py` gives the smoke a pass/fail verdict instead of an eyeball, checking all three required properties; property 3 runs the **real** offline scorer rather than a proxy, because (1) and (2) can both hold while every answer still strips to nothing. Per-cell parse-failure budget is the scorer's own 2, not a looser smoke-only threshold; an empty ledger fails rather than passing by vacuous truth. **Negative control already run**: against a *copy* of the historic W0 Gemma run it fails all three properties and exits 1 (430/430 empty answers, 0 reasoning fields, 43/43 parse failures in each of 10 cells) — copy, not the historic dir, since the scorer writes into the run dir and history is appended, never edited. Confirms the precise W0 mechanism: HTTP 200, `predicted_n=64`, `response_text=""` — the old parser read only `content`/`delta.content` while gemma emits `reasoning_content`, so the answer channel captured nothing and the reasoning was never persisted anywhere (hence "no raw SSE ledger"). Smoke manifest `data/batched_decode/e5_manifests_w2_capture_smoke/` uses the registered C1 (1×full+interleave) W2 shape at the Stage-B 256-token cap, production sampling, pinned 43-question batch, `decision_grade_intent=false`. 8 new tests, ruff clean. **The smoke itself still needs an inference window — it has not been run.**

**E5 Stage-B COMPLETE ✅ 2026-07-29 — 31 cells, three model groups, 0.0% error on every cell, 26/31 decision-grade.** Runs `e5-w1-qwen36-20260729T154725Z` (11 cells, 9 DG), `e5-w4-80b-20260729T165639Z` (12, 10 DG), `e5-w2-gemma-20260729T183151Z` (8, 7 DG). No `--allow-host-health-warning`, no `--skip-clean-check`, zero host-health warnings, host released 18:45:19Z with zero orphans. **HEADLINE: C3 (four quarters) loses at every clean iso-T rung in all three groups** — W1 C2@8 > C1@16 by 29.3%; W2 C1 > C3 by 40.0% (T=8) and 47.5% (T=16); W4 C1b@4 > C3@2 by 26.5%, tie at T=16. The *winning* shape is model-dependent — 35B wants one half, gemma one full machine + interleave, 80B two node-local halves — which is itself the slot-fabric finding. **Evidence for a provisioning decision, not the decision**: one pass per cell, T=32 pending offline re-derivation. The local operator artifact was updated in place with the W0 grids retained verbatim.

**R1's basis caveat is PRESENTATIONAL — a consumer cannot see it** ✅ 2026-07-29 (auditor-verified at the line). `server_numa_np_sweep.py:2162` sets `mixed_metric_basis`; `:2163-2168` attaches a note whose own words are *"verdict caveated, not decision-grade"*; then `:2172-2181` sets `status = "winner"` **without ever reading the flag**. It reaches output only at `:2695`, appended to the human-readable summary line — so a human reading prose sees the caveat while a consumer joining on `status`/`winner_config` ingests a caveated verdict as decision-grade. **Fix shape (instrument code, human-gated, not applied):** when the flag is true, `status` must not be plain `winner` — emit `winner_caveated` or `insufficient_data`, changing the field a consumer keys on while keeping the margin and note. Same class as the day's other findings: *the instrument knows; the output does not carry the knowledge.*

**E5 W1-W4 runs — UNBLOCKED (reboot landed); awaiting an exclusive inference window** — the `BLOCKED_ON_OPERATOR_SCHEDULED_REBOOT` gate is **lifted** (host rebooted 2026-07-29 ~13:42Z; uptime well inside the P-BENCH decision-grade window). All prep is complete and dry-run-verified — see the two ✅ items above and the runbook `epyc-inference-research/data/batched_decode/E5_STAGE_B_RUNBOOK.md`. Remaining blocker is **scheduling, not readiness**: E5 decision-grade is mutually exclusive with ANY llama-server on the host (`host_health_warnings()` counts `existing_llama_processes` **unfiltered**; `--coexist-allow-pattern` relaxes only `ensure_clean_runtime` and teardown, not the health gate — enforced at run start **and** per-cell mid-run, so a stack bringup mid-window kills the remaining cells). Do **not** pass `--allow-host-health-warning`/`--skip-clean-check` here: both force `decision_grade=false` for the whole run (they were correct for W0 at 20-day uptime; they are wrong now). Original text retained below for the record. ORIGINALLY: **BLOCKED_ON_OPERATOR_SCHEDULED_REBOOT** — all W0-derived execution prep is complete, but operator-scheduled reboot remains a hard P-BENCH-1/3 boundary. After reboot, run W1-W4 only in the quiet window; W2 additionally requires its focused post-fix capture smoke. R1-R4 remain withheld until clean decision-grade Stage-B cells exist.

**ROOT CAUSE FOUND — E5 measured through a straddling-cpuset NUMA defect; all Stage-B + W0 throughput SUSPENDED** ✅ 2026-07-30 — the swept placement shapes inherit the production wiring's defect: `stack_numa.py:66-67` `NUMA_NODE0 = "0-47,96-143"` / `NUMA_NODE1 = "48-95,144-191"` each straddle a **pair** of NPS4 nodes (`node0 = 0-23,96-119`, `node1 = 24-47,120-143`, `node2 = 48-71,144-167`, `node3 = 72-95,168-191`) and are launched with **no `numactl --interleave`**, so weights first-touch onto a single node and the other node's threads pay a remote-access penalty on every weight read — the E5 affinity artifact for this shape recorded `pages_by_node {N0: 9226101} / total 9226101`, all 35.2 GiB on node0 under a node0+node1 thread team. **`--interleave` binds at FIRST TOUCH only**, hence a silent no-op against a warm page cache: the defect survives casual checking and a warm re-test appears to confirm the bad number. **Quantified** (`llama-bench` tg128, no spec-dec, `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-Q8_0`): straddling+no-interleave **warm = the current production wiring** `7.81 ± 3.82` t/s; same cold `10.28`; straddling **+interleave** cold `-t 96` `15.35`; **full machine `taskset -c 0-95` + `numactl --interleave=all` cold `-t 96` = `23.43 ± 0.07`** — a **3.0×** gap, i.e. Stage-B priced the frontdoor model at ~one third of its true speed. With MTP spec-dec ON at the winning placement, single stream measures **36-39** t/s, independently matching the AutoPilot production anchor (`median_request_tps` median **35.7**, n=154, band 35-40). **Instrument sound**: a single-NPS4-node arm (24 physical cores, `-t 48`) measured `8.80` vs the registry-documented `8.90` — 1% match. **Ruled out**: v8 kernel regression (v7 and v8 both `9.76`, identical), iqk (never engages for Q8_0 — gated behind an unset `GGML_IQK_Q8_0`), MTP head overhead, mmap page-faulting. Suspension notice + per-block retraction markers landed at the top of this handoff; suspended numbers retained verbatim per the append-never-edit rule.

**RE-MEASURE E5 Stage-B on the corrected placement** — re-run the 31-cell Stage-B grid (W1 `qwen36_q8_0`, W2 gemma, W4 `qwen3_next_80b`) with correct NUMA policy per shape, then re-derive R1-R4. Binding requirements: (a) **add full machine `0-95` + `numactl --interleave=all` as a swept shape for `qwen36_q8_0` and `qwen3_next_80b`** — today's winner was present in the old grid only as gemma's `C1`, so the qwen36/80B grids could not have found it; (b) every straddling-cpuset cell must either carry `--interleave` or be declared as an explicit defect-replication control, never left implicit; (c) **`drop_caches` before every cell and record `pages_by_node`** — `--interleave` is a no-op on a warm cache, so a warm cell silently measures the defect; (d) attest the numactl policy per instance alongside the existing affinity preflight, and fail closed when policy and cpuset disagree; (e) reuse the existing harness unchanged (it is not implicated — see SURVIVES in the notice) so the re-run stays comparable, and re-check the still-open T=32 `empty_trimmed_window` and R2/R4 mixed-basis items above against the new runs. Needs an exclusive inference window under the same clean-window terms as Stage-B.

**Fix the production cpuset wiring in `stack_numa.py` (orchestrator; gated on the re-measurement)** — `frontdoor` idx0 (port 8070) and `ingest_long_context` idx0 (port 8085) both pin `NUMA_NODE0 = "0-47,96-143"` with **no `numactl_policy`**, which is the defective shape measured at `7.81` t/s warm. `eval_batch_frontdoor` (18070) uses the same cpuset but does carry `interleave=all`; `worker_general` (8083) already uses `NUMA_FULL` + `interleave=all` and is unaffected. **The justification comment in the file is invalid evidence**: the April 2026-04-17 head-to-head (`26.60` interleave vs `27.06` NUMA_NODE0, "B beats A by 1.7%") predates the 2026-04-24 NPS4 reboot — the cpuset genuinely WAS one node then — and its source CSV records `spec == "baseline"`, i.e. speculative decoding OFF. `ingest_long_context` cites that same dead head-to-head to "keep parity" and inherits the defect with no data of its own. The `NUMA_NODE0`/`NUMA_NODE1` names are NPS2-era artefacts and have been misleading since the NPS4 reboot; the `NUMA_Q*` quarters are correctly named and ARE the four NPS4 nodes. **Status: annotated in place 2026-07-30, change deliberately NOT applied** — the wiring is held unchanged so the re-measurement stays comparable with the recorded AutoPilot operating point being re-anchored against. Production serving-path change → operator-gated; apply only once the corrected Stage-B reports.

**Retract the suspended figures in the operator-facing E5 artifact** — the authoritative local HTML (`artifacts/operator/e5_w0_preliminary_results.html`) carries the Stage-B headline and therefore still presents retracted numbers. Add the suspension banner and the "C3 never wins" retraction while retaining the figures verbatim (append-only). Do not regenerate it from the superseded markdown.

files.title: Batched Structured Editing + Parallel Apply Fan-out

boxes.text: **BEP-1 — Batch-edit mode (think-then-act).** ✅ 2026-05-26 (flipped 2026-07-14; wired `ea5f010` behind `features().batch_edit_mode`, pure pieces done+tested). Add a coder/architect mode that produces a complete structured patch set (per-file hunks) in one shot after a bounded evidence-gathering phase, with no edit/apply tool calls interleaved through the reasoning chain. Define the patch schema as deterministic data, not free-form XML-only prose: `base_repo_sha`, per-file `path`, `base_content_sha256`, `operation`, hunks with line anchors or unified-diff body, expected postconditions, and declared cross-file dependencies. Reuse TOON for compact transport if useful, but validate into a typed Python object before touching disk. Default-off feature flag.

**BEP-2 / J8 — CPU latency A/B for the legacy structured patchset path.** Head-to-head bench: batch-edit mode vs interleaved Root LM loop on a coding/edit workload — measure round-trip count, total prefill tokens, end-to-end latency, bundle/context size if DCP is enabled, patch-parse failure rate, apply failure rate, verification pass rate, and quality. This no longer gates practical multi-file coding remediation because the separate `force_mode="edit"` transaction has already solved that blocker. Run BEP-2/J8 only if its answer would change whether the legacy `batch_edit_mode` patchset path is kept, retired, or exposed as a narrow task-class knob. First run an offline replay with already-known patches to estimate deterministic apply overhead; then run inference. *(Inference-gated — prepare commands, user runs; standalone llama-bench only for raw speed per `feedback_speed_verify_via_llama_bench`.)*

**BEP-3 — Autopilot search-space knob.** If BEP-2 is positive, expose batch-vs-interleaved as a StructuralLab boolean (or per-role/per-task-class knob) so autopilot can find where each wins. Wires into autopilot-continuous-optimization search space. The knob must be task-class aware because run-test-iterate tasks may require interleaving while mechanical multi-file edits may benefit from batching.

**BEP-4 — Parallel apply fan-out.** ✅ 2026-06-28 (flipped 2026-07-14; deterministic stage-local fan-out live; LM-repair lane tracked below). Given a BEP-1 patch set, first try deterministic patch application in parallel by file/process with no additional LM calls. Only if deterministic apply fails should an optional cheap-worker repair lane run, and that lane must be explicitly inference-gated. Collect per-file results; surface a combined reviewable diff plus a machine-readable failure manifest. Reuse the 32×6t concurrent-split harness for CPU parallelism, but preserve a dependency graph: files with declared cross-file ordering constraints or generated-code dependencies must serialize within their group.

**BEP-5 — Sandbox-before-disk + granular accept/reject (general).** Generalize Meta-Harness Tier-2's git-commit-before / ast-validate discipline beyond the 4-file allowlist into a general "stage in sandbox/worktree → reviewable diff → independent verify → accept/reject per file or hunk → commit" apply path. Safety-gated — design most carefully (autonomous general code edits). Use base-hash preconditions to reject stale patches, forbid edits outside the declared scope, and always run a whole-repo verification pass after per-file verification because cross-file errors are invisible to isolated checks.

**BEP-4 telemetry hardening — typed verifier failures.** `apply_patchset_sandboxed()` now records `FailureType.VERIFY_FAILED` when an explicit verifier returns false without raising, preserving the machine-readable failure manifest expected by BEP-4/BEP-2 reports. Focused runner/hook tests passed (`34 passed`) and ruff was clean. ✅ 2026-07-06

**BEP-4 residual — optional LM-repair lane.** When deterministic apply fails, run an optional cheap-worker repair lane (explicitly inference-gated, opt-in per `feedback_no_concurrent_inference`). Only remaining BEP-4 piece after the 2026-06-28 deterministic fan-out landed.

**BEP-6 — hashline vs `current_shas`: the granularity gap does not exist** (intake-1148#record, intake-1150#record, intake-1153, intake-1154) ✅ 2026-08-18. The Stage-1 premise — that hashline is line-granularity optimistic concurrency where ours is file-granularity — is **OVERTURNED**. Current hashline validates ONE 4-hex xxHash32 of the whole normalized file (`packages/hashline/src/format.ts:112-121`) and addresses lines by plain number; per-line hashes were removed in `30793c165`/`7c6457652` (May 2026). That is the same property `current_shas` already gives us. Two leniency details worth knowing if we ever revisit: the hash normalizes away trailing whitespace (a stale file differing only in trailing whitespace is ACCEPTED), and a 16-bit tag misses a stale edit ~1 in 65,536. **No change to our apply path is proposed.**

**BEP-7 — if an edit-format change is ever proposed, apply two external rules first.** (a) **PAIRING RULE** (intake-1154, aider): a format change without a matching *tolerant applier* is a different intervention — disabling flexible patching produced a **9x increase in editing errors** on aider's own benchmark. (b) **LINE-NUMBER TENSION** (intake-1153, Cursor): line-number emission is named as a tokenizer-level failure mode — a digit run tokenized as one token forces a single-forward-pass commit — and Cursor adopted aider search/replace blocks specifically to remove it. Both predate hashline; omp's shipped format moved *toward* line numbers with no published benchmark of it. Resolve by measurement, not authority. **Decision-relevant magnitude:** against `str_replace`, hashline's measured mean is **+2.97 pp** (14/19 models, sign p=0.064) — inside the benchmark's own 3.75 pp median test-retest spread. ONNX checker accepts both graphs with inputs `input_ids`/`attention_mask` and output `token_embeddings`; parity vs PyLate passed with max cosine divergence `2.7212e-03` and mean `1.2388e-03` at tolerance `1e-2`. Follow-up `epyc-orchestrator` `7c1e41e` adds `onnxscript` to the export preflight and makes reranker availability require actual model loadability instead of file presence only.

**S4c**: CPU latency benchmark with Reason-mxbai INT8 at 48 threads for 10 snippets (~30 min). Target median ≤80 ms. **Harness prereq DONE 2026-06-14**: `epyc-orchestrator` `b37de4a` added `scripts/benchmark/bench_colbert_rerank.py` with warmup-separated latency metrics, JSON output, explicit LateOn/Reason-mxbai model-slot overrides, and no-model skip behavior. **Measured 2026-06-14** on the real ONNX Runtime path after `7c1e41e` hardened availability checks: artifact `/mnt/raid0/llm/models/reason-mxbai-colbert-v0-32m-onnx-int8`, 50 measured calls, 5 warmup calls, 10 snippets/call, median `104.434 ms`, mean `104.301 ms`, p95 `105.237 ms`, first call `107.838 ms`, throughput `95.876 snippets/s`. Result: latency is faster than the older ~180 ms GTE baseline but misses the original ≤80 ms target; treat Reason-mxbai as promising-but-not-yet-accepted until request-path A/B and any optimization pass. **Superseded 2026-08-12** — that 104 ms was an unbounded-ONNX-thread-pool measurement; with the intra-op bound the same harness reads **49.1 ms**, inside the ≤80 ms gate. See "S4b measurement (2026-08-12)" below.

**S5-amend**: **LANDED 2026-06-14** in `epyc-orchestrator` `107a8db`. `src/tools/web/colbert_reranker.py` now has a three-slot selector documented in code comments: `LATEON_MODEL_PATH` primary, `REASON_MXBAI_MODEL_PATH` 32M fallback, and GTE-ModernColBERT-v1 default. Unit coverage verifies default, Reason-mxbai-only, and LateOn-over-Reason precedence. Full A/B remains inference-gated on AR-3 Package D, same gate as S5.

**G14 (compute-gated) — re-export `Reason-mxbai-colbert-v0-32m` with `pylate-onnx-export` 1.7.0 so the slot finally has an `onnx_config.json`.** The staged artifact at `/mnt/raid0/llm/models/reason-mxbai-colbert-v0-32m-onnx-int8` ships `config_sentence_transformers.json` but **no `onnx_config.json`** — the file the NextPlaid Rust reader requires and the one `colbert_encoder._load_declared_config()` now prefers (`epyc-orchestrator` `4e5e84c0`). Install **from git**: `pip install "pylate-onnx-export @ git+https://github.com/lightonai/next-plaid.git#subdirectory=next-plaid-onnx/python"` — **not** the model card's `onnx/python` path, which 404s at head and at `00e26aae`, and **not** PyPI 0.1.0, which takes the projection from `pylate_model[1].linear` while reading the output dimension from `pylate_model[-1]`: on this **3-Dense** checkpoint (`1_Dense` 384→768, `2_Dense` 768→768, `3_Dense` 768→128) that emits a **truncated graph with a mislabelled `embedding_dim`**. Pin a PyLate ceiling as well — `query_prefix_id` gained a `None` return at 1.6.0 that `export.py:264-265`'s bare `int()` would crash on. **Compute is one CPU trace of a 32M model — seconds.** **Owning handoff**: this one (`colbert-reranker-web-research.md`). **What opens the gate**: the real blocker is an **environment prerequisite, not compute** — 1.7.0 declares `requires-python ">=3.10,<3.13"` and this host is Python 3.13.7, so a **Python 3.10–3.12 venv must exist first**. Once it does, the gate opens when the exported graph's declared `embedding_dim` matches the last Dense's `out_features` (**128** here) **and** parity holds against the existing **92 MB** (92,079,820 B) `model_int8.onnx`. The older cp314 / `fast-plaid` / `voyager` objection on file is **stale**: `voyager` is an optional extra gated `python_version < 3.14`, `fast-plaid` ships cp310–cp314 manylinux wheels, and `pylate/__init__.py` never imports `pylate/indexes/`, so neither is imported on this path.

Add a 2-D preference vector `ω = (ω_perf, ω_cost)` on the simplex (`ω_perf + ω_cost = 1`) read from request metadata (default ω = (0.5, 0.5)).

Add calibrated cost scaling parameter τ as a runtime knob (env var `DAR_COST_TAU`, default 1.0; canonical env `ORCHESTRATOR_MEMRL_RETRIEVAL_COST_TAU` takes precedence). τ multiplies the normalized-cost penalty.

Inference-time score: `selection_score = 2 * (ω_perf * Q(prompt, model) - ω_cost * cost_lambda * τ * normalized_cost(model))`. The default `ω=(0.5,0.5), τ=1.0` preserves the existing `Q - cost_lambda * normalized_cost` selector exactly.

**DAR-5.3**: Augment `v_prompt` with the IRT 2-D output concatenated to the BGE embedding. New `v_prompt = [BGE_embedding | irt_difficulty | irt_discrimination]`.
**DAR-5.4**: A/B against frozen-DAR-4 (hard-coded features) on val set. Decision gate: if IRT+identity-vectors improves routing accuracy by ≥ 2 points val acc, promote to default.

Per-backend failures (exceptions OR `success=False` results) are caught and surfaced as `SwarmCompletion(success=False, error=...)` rather than crashing the dispatch. **URE-1 — Uncertainty-quantified escalation signal.** Add a calibrated decision-uncertainty estimate as an escalation trigger *orthogonal* to the quality Q-value. Candidate inputs: routing classifier confidence/entropy, top-2 margin, Q-value spread, conformal abstention score, MC-dropout variance if enabled, and disagreement between rule/router/Q-scorer. Gated on URE-1 calibration quality and an ablation showing uncertainty improves routing or escalation decisions beyond existing difficulty/risk features. Start in shadow mode; do not let uncertainty recursively train itself without frozen labels.

**DCP-1 — Context bundle data model + per-file inclusion modes.** ✅ 2026-05-26 (flipped 2026-07-14; on main, tested — see status quo). Define a `ContextBundle` with per-entry `mode ∈ {full, slices, codemap_only}`, merged line-range slices (auto-merge overlapping/adjacent ranges), and a live token-count accumulator. Each entry MUST carry: `path`, `mode`, `line_ranges`, `symbol_ids` where available, `content_sha256`, `source` (`gitnexus|colgrep|direct_read|manual_seed`), `reason_included`, `reason_downgraded_or_excluded`, and `estimated_tokens`. Reuse GitNexus for `codemap_only`, ColGREP/read for `slices`/`full`. Store the bundle manifest separately from rendered prompt text so downstream roles can request top-ups against stable IDs instead of asking for "that file again." *(Substrate for everything else; net-new.)*

**DCP-2 — Budget-bounded assembly loop.** ✅ 2026-05-26 (flipped 2026-07-14; discovery+pack core on main, tested). Given a sub-task description + token budget, run discover → codemap → token-verify → add/drop/slice until the bundle fits; emit the bundle + a manifest of what was included/excluded and why. **Budget is a per-role parameter, NOT a fixed 60k** — ours is set by the receiving role's context window and the CPU latency target, not a cloud paste ceiling. Implement as a two-pass loop for efficiency: first pass uses only cheap metadata (GitNexus graph, file sizes, symbol names, ColGREP candidate IDs); second pass reads bodies only for files that survive ranking. Reserve explicit budget bands before packing: task/instructions, codemap, editable slices/full files, tests/examples, and an output reserve. Fail closed if the estimate cannot fit after slicing: emit `codemap_only` + "missing evidence" manifest rather than silently overflowing.

**DCP-3 — CodeMaps-as-budget-class.** ✅ 2026-05-26 (flipped 2026-07-14; ast-codemap on main, tested; GitNexus not a runtime dep). Add a GitNexus-backed "architecture snapshot" producer: signature-only skeletons for a symbol/file set, sized to a sub-budget, injected as a distinct section. *(Closes the "analyzed-not-wired" gap — GitNexus can already do this, nothing exposes it for prompt injection.)* Cache codemaps by `(path, content_sha256, gitnexus_index_commit)` and expose staleness in the manifest. If `gitnexus status` is stale, either run the wrapper re-index before assembly or mark codemap confidence low and prefer direct slices for changed files.

**DCP-4 — Wire pre-assembly into delegation as a seed bundle, not a hard context firewall.** WIRED 2026-05-26 (`31ea6d4`), behind `features().dcp_pre_assembly` (default-off). Attach point is `chat_delegation._run_specialist_loop` (the LIVE specialist delegation path — NOT `dispatcher.py`, which only generates the plan/commands): after `corpus_ctx` is built, `_maybe_dcp_seed_context()` augments it with `render_bundle(assemble_delegation_bundle(query, code_search_fn=deleg_repl._code_search, file_reader_fn=...))`. Added `context_discovery.render_bundle()` (the missing body-materialization step — the bundle only planned modes). **Advisory**: reactive discovery stays fully enabled; any failure falls back to plain `corpus_ctx` (never blocks delegation). 7 tests. *(Top-up-rate eval signal + manifest-in-prompt are DCP-6-era refinements; the seed currently renders bodies only.)* Remaining: offline replay + DCP-6 inference A/B (deferred to post-J6).

**DCP-5 — Non-prescriptive discovery prompt.** Landed in `epyc-orchestrator` `b7ba6265`: `architect_investigate` now frames supplied context as an evidence bundle, asks delegation briefs to identify open questions, file relationships, missing evidence, and omitted-file uncertainty, and avoids prescribing implementation details before discovery. This is prompt-surface only, not a PromptForge A/B promotion; keep DCP-6 quality/latency evidence as the enablement gate.

**DCP-6 — Eval.** Measure on a delegation-heavy workload: prefill tokens, end-to-end latency, top-up count, bundle-build latency, downstream answer quality, hallucinated-file references, and context-contamination failures vs the reactive-discovery baseline. Hypothesis: budget-bounded pre-assembly cuts prefill + latency at equal-or-better quality. Non-inference replay over historical tasks closed 2026-06-12 for task-root/file-selection/budget correctness; DCP-6a live-branch commit `2e2e0d3` fixes shallow one-line slices and manifest freshness hashes and replays clean. Launch-code provenance is satisfied (`server_launch_git_sha=eeb8cce`, current API `git_sha=27e09a1`), but orchestrator `670aab4` records a caveated running-state attestation. Orchestrator `29b9ba3` adds the executable A/B harness (`python3 scripts/benchmark/dcp_j7_ab.py --stub ...` for schema/artifact validation; real mode requires `--host-quiet-confirmed` and refuses if AutoPilot is running). First live A/B artifact landed at `benchmarks/results/runs/dcp_j7/20260619T113143Z/` in orchestrator `56a72f6` after `f96a6ab` fixed cached-delegation telemetry; it completed cleanly but did not support promotion (`on.p50_elapsed_s=32.628` vs `off.p50_elapsed_s=20.219`, `on.avg_tokens_generated=247.333` vs `off.avg_tokens_generated=352.0`, zero errors). The artifact summary now records `decision.status=hold` because latency regressed and rows were not quality-scored. Orchestrator `c3b2514e` makes attestation report this status directly in JSON/Markdown (`## DCP/J7 Status`). Remaining work is larger/quality-scored falsification and broad operational attestation cleanup before any enablement.

**DCP-6b — J7 runner no-inference safety revalidation.** ✅ 2026-07-06 — Orchestrator `7c84f102` makes stub/schema validation the default runner mode, requires explicit `--real --host-quiet-confirmed` for live inference, and records `benchmarks/results/runs/dcp_j7/stub-20260706T033205Z/` as a current schema artifact.

**DCP-7 — external evidence that MORE CONTEXT IS NOT MONOTONICALLY BETTER** (intake-1152, EDIT-Bench, arXiv:2511.04486v2 Table 3). First external number we hold for what a context field is worth on an editing task, and it points *against* naive enrichment. Seven models, three context levels (code only / +highlight / +highlight+cursor): claude-sonnet-4 62.41 / 64.81 / 64.26; glm-4.6 52.96 / 56.48 / **44.81 (−8.15)**; o3-mini 60.00 / **56.30 (−3.70)** / 55.19; qwen3-coder 56.48 / **53.89 (−2.59)**. Highlighting helps 5 of 7 and HURTS 2; adding cursor position on top costs one model 8.15 pp. The abstract's "up to 11%" is glm-4.6's within-model range, not a typical effect — typical is 2-4 pp. **Read-across:** DCP assembles context budgets on the assumption that relevant context helps; this says a *relevant-looking* field can be per-model negative at single-digit-pp magnitude. Not decision-gating (different task, different models) — a prior worth holding before the next budget change.

**DCP-8 — borrow the paired descriptive/lazy instruction axis** (intake-1157, CanItEdit) as an instrument for prompt-construction work, where instruction specificity currently varies uncontrolled: every problem carries a fully-specified AND a minimal instruction, making specificity a controlled variable rather than a confound. Pairs with CJ-7c in `canonical-judge-suite-revamp.md`; filed here because DCP owns the instruction-assembly side.

**DCP-9a — Compute the Eq.-4 quantities over the existing Claude Code journals** (do now, zero compute): cache-read fraction `h`, cache-creation share, uncached-input share, input:output ratio, per-session token intensity, and the Definition-1 trajectory test over time. First-pass numbers are already in hand and dive-verified: **61 transcripts, 45,902 usage records, h = 0.9845, input:output 350.5:1**. This **supersedes and sharpens** the bearing row "measure coordination overhead as a fraction of mains' token spend from existing journals" — the ~60%/95% figure remains a budget whose artifact is absent, and no baseline of our own exists. `intake-1333#00`, `intake-1325#04` (the unsplit ancestor).

**DCP-9b — The coordination SHARE is NOT computable from journals as they stand.** This is an **instrumentation** task, not a measurement task: it needs the per-turn PURPOSE LABEL written at write time (P5-3 in [`loop-owned-fleet-implementation.md`](loop-owned-fleet-implementation.md)), never post-hoc classification of transcripts. **Depends on P5-3.** `intake-1333#00`. Zero compute.

(Gated) Add the ColBERT KB as an optional prior-decisions source in delegation-context pre-assembly, behind the existing `dcp_pre_assembly` flag; measure quality/latency before default-on (DCP's live A/B is already latency-unfavorable: ON 32.6s vs OFF 20.2s)

**DCP-10 — Zero-decode discovery scoring on ContextBench (primary instrument).** Per instance: shallow checkout at `base_commit` (`CONTEXTBENCH_TMP_ROOT` on raid, never /tmp), run `discover_candidates` (`context_discovery.py:87`) with `ORCHESTRATOR_EDIT_ROOT` at the checkout; emit `pred_files`+`pred_spans` from `DiscoveredHit.line_ranges`, and separately the post-`pack_to_budget` spans. Score File and Line recall/precision/F1 **macro per task**, plus recall at the live 2000-token budget and at 2x/4x. Start Lite Python (266) + all C/C++ (128). Arms at fixed `max_files`: (a) task-root lexical; (b) ColGREP; (c) ColGREP + 1-hop GitNexus edges (conf ≥0.9) appended; (d) same edges re-rank-only; (e) `ripwire --for/--pack-task` at a pinned SHA. **Wrap the shipped scorer first** (it micro-averages, drops errored/empty predictions, scores empty gold/pred as 1.0, mangles dot-paths via `lstrip("./")`, EditLoc falls back to the gold patch, parses `.h` as C): count errors/empty as recall 0, exclude the 3 empty-gold and 42 `/workspace`-scratch-file tasks, flag the third-party-audit-reported 88 unresolvable-path tasks (count not re-verified), prefix-strip paths, drop EditLoc, omit Symbol for C/C++. Requires DCP-10a for the C/C++ arm. `intake-1366#record`, `intake-1364#record`, `intake-1346#record`.

**DCP-10-SCORE-PREP (NI05-38)** ✅ 2026-10-05 — prepare pure deterministic macro file/span precision/recall/F1, safe checkout-relative path normalization and unioned inclusive ranges; preserve error/empty prediction denominators and explicit immutable task dispositions. Report actual deterministic packer output at 2k/4k/8k with full/slice/codemap line provenance and estimated-token identity. Hand-checked synthetic fixtures only. No acquisition, checkouts, index/model builds, actual discovery arms or full-benchmark claim. Prospective exclusive scored-report request/original-output/input/source custody is VB-CONTEXTBENCH-SCORE-WIRE; shared verifier grade only, descriptive score fields, no historical backfill.

**DCP-10a — Close the C/C++ gap in task-root discovery.** ✅ 2026-09-14 — merged to epyc-orchestrator main `35b05fde` (pushed to origin 2026-09-14) (commit `982ca87c`, test `test_code_search_discovers_cpp_and_systems_language_files`). The task-root whitelist lacked `.c/.cc/.cpp/.h/.hpp/.go/.rs/.java`; now covered (plus `.cxx`). Codemap stays `.py`-only (`context_discovery.py:205,279`), so the C/C++ arm scores discovery, not codemaps. `intake-1366#record`.

**DCP-10b — Secondary Python ranking cross-check on Loc-Bench V1** (after DCP-10): Acc@5/@10 file + Function Acc@10 on the `discover_candidates` ordering with `evaluate_results(dataset="czlll/Loc-Bench_V1")`; strip `.__init__`; raise `max_files` to ≥10; report bug-only (post-Oct-2024) vs all. Rows stay in scratch, never committed; exclude the 10 MULocBench-flagged invalid instances and issue-#24 instances; define our own frozen split (do NOT reuse ripwire's salted "held-out" slices — its split was re-partitioned by a rename). `intake-1356#record`, `intake-1346#04`.

**DCP-10c — ripwire vs GitNexus blast-radius head-to-head (evidence only).** Pinned ripwire SHA vs current GitNexus (upgrade from 1.6.8 first) on epyc-orchestrator + epyc-root; pre-authored frozen questions weighted to callers/impact/context; GitNexus run with its intended impact/context workflow; commit questions, raw outputs and scoring; judge outside both projects. The external 27W/7L/14T is single-judge, uncommitted and CLI-only-GitNexus — not evidence. **CLAUDE.md is human-only (`human_only_paths.yaml`); any change to the gitnexus-before-edit rule needs an operator token.** `intake-1346#03`.

**DCP-11 — Packer rendering: stop downgrading edit-site files to signatures.** For a candidate with ColGREP hit line-ranges, never render `codemap_only`; keep the hit AST segments verbatim (+ class headers/imports) and render other segments as `# ... N lines omitted`, or exclude with a "missing evidence" manifest entry. `test_pack_includes_high_priority_full_then_downgrades` encodes today's downgrade and must change with it. Policy change → validate as a DCP-6 arm (ON vs current) after DCP-12. `intake-1357#record`, `intake-1365#record`.

**DCP-12 — DCP-6 power prerequisite.** Before any DCP-6 rerun: ≥2 identical-arm reruns of the same role+prompt set to measure the local run-to-run flip rate, then size the paired sample for exact McNemar. n=3/arm cannot resolve effects under an ~9%-class flip floor (6/70 flips on a T=0 cloud API). `intake-1357#04`.

**DCP-13 — Delegation hand-off fidelity.** Code facts at orchestrator `5a9442d3`: the architect decision loop breaks on turn 0 in every branch (`chat_delegation.py:203-220`) so the advertised `fetch_report` is unreachable; D|Approved and the `skip_synthesis_on_timeout` early return can hand handle+summary text to the user; `worker_summarize` runs even for rescued reports whose summary is discarded. Zero-compute half DONE 2026-09-14 — merged to epyc-orchestrator main `35b05fde` (pushed to origin 2026-09-14): `2bffb45b` removes the dead `fetch_report` advertisement from the synthesis prompt and `review.py` fallback; `57ceb7d5` returns full reports on D|Approved, the timeout early return and four other user-facing returns (architect-error early returns, forced-synthesis failure fallback, `needs_input` partial); `a2af42ad` skips `worker_summarize` on rescued reports while still persisting the handle. **Residual (open):** `_to_report_handle_text` (`chat_delegation_reports.py`) still writes "Use fetch_report('<id>')" into handle text the architect cannot act on; delegation-cache hits on non-rescued runs still return the handle+summary form.

**DCP-13a — Drop or make actionable the `fetch_report` line in handle text.** `_to_report_handle_text` (`chat_delegation_reports.py`) still writes "Use fetch_report('<id>') for full content." into text the architect cannot act on (turn-0 break); update the report-handle integration test with it. Zero compute.

**DCP-13b — Cache hits return the short form.** On non-rescued runs the delegation cache stores handle+summary text, so a later cache hit hands the user that form; store the full report (or reload it from the handle) on the user-facing path. Zero compute. Inference-gated arms stay open here: (i) label confident-wrong outcomes where the stored raw report held the evidence but summary/answer dropped it (arms: summary+handle vs raw vs verbatim rescue); (ii) index-backed seed bundle with NO specialist delegation vs delegation; (iii) explored-vs-used evidence drop (seed bundle = step 0) against the ≤20% top-up rule. `intake-1358#record`, `intake-1366#record`.

boxes.text: **Do NOT port cosine-top-1 retrieval. Layer CORE's (intake-888) utility-aware retrieval over ReasoningBank's schema.** Convergent evidence: the k-ablation loses **half the benefit by k=4** (49.7 / 46.0 / 45.5 / 44.4), and the one independent 35B replication **failed specifically at the RETRIEVER** after an embedder swap — exactly the substitution we would make with local BGE. Treat **k as a measured parameter**, with **k=1** and **episodic-only** control arms.

**Rider on the k-parameter above: k must be BUDGET-CONDITIONAL, not fixed.** intake-936 (independent, DeepSeek-V3.2 backbone) finds six of fifteen memory methods scoring **below** the no-memory baseline at a **128K** budget — mechanism is **context-budget competition**, not store growth (do **not** conflate with intake-899). So the retrieval sweep must vary k **as a fraction of remaining window budget**, and include a no-memory control arm, or it will select a k that is optimal only at short context.

**ReasoningBank ranking correction:** do not carry “best overall” into retrieval design. intake-936 places it last of 13 on Cross-Episode Knowledge (Easy); its schema/store shape, not ranking, is the transferable signal. **W5 — STM as generated view** (impl 4.1, ~1–2 days, needs W1): `short_term_memory.md` rebuilt each trial from the ledger (trustworthy last-N, hypotheses with falsifiers + provenance trial-ids); read-modify-write path deleted; per-section render budgets (kills mid-word truncation structurally). **Pre-cutover scaffold landed 2026-06-14** in `epyc-orchestrator` `fbef7a8`: `scripts/autopilot/stm_generated_view.py` renders a journal-derived read-only preview from folded entries, mirrors AP-22 trust filters by excluding bug-corrupted, non-`ok`, and learning-excluded rows, sanitizes legacy failure text, splits optimization directions deterministically, applies section and total budget caps, and prints to stdout only. **Journal-path hardening landed 2026-06-14** in `e5205b1`: an explicit missing or non-directory `--journal-dir` now exits with code `2` before constructing `ExperimentJournal`, so a typo does not create directories; valid existing explicit journal directories still render. **Live prompt-memory generation landed 2026-06-18** in `cfa8525`: AutoPilot startup, planner prompt construction, and post-journal trial finalization now call `ShortTermMemory.refresh_from_journal(...)`, which renders the folded append-only journal view and atomically writes the generated projection. **Legacy mutable STM cleanup landed 2026-06-18** in `3c3e016`: `TrialOutcome`, `ShortTermMemory.update()`, and the read-modify-write accumulator internals were removed; `ShortTermMemory` now only maintains the generated journal projection. **Tracked-runtime-artifact policy landed 2026-06-18** in `91d074d`: the generated projection moved to ignored `orchestration/autopilot_short_term_memory.md`, and tracked `scripts/autopilot/short_term_memory.md` was removed from source control.

`EvolutionManager.distill()` validates those IDs against the analyzed rows, permits only the single-row fallback for one-row distillations, skips ungrounded multi-trial insights, and returns `status: skipped` if no grounded insight remains. **Promotion evidence propagation landed 2026-06-14** in `433f6e8`: `KnowledgeDistiller` reads evidence IDs from source rows and carries them through raw-to-pattern and pattern-to-convention promotions, so retrieval quarantine by excluded evidence IDs also hides promoted pattern/convention rows whose underlying evidence is superseded or excluded. **Folded evidence-view centralization landed 2026-06-18/19** in `327218c` and `de07542`: `excluded_strategy_evidence_trial_ids()` is the shared quarantine helper, `StrategyStore.retrieve_for_journal()` computes exclusions from the supplied journal, and `_build_mutation_context()` routes through that wrapper with a legacy-test-double fallback. **Convention audit-table evidence propagation landed 2026-06-19** in `5544a6e`: dedicated `strategy_conventions` audit rows now store, migrate, list, and propagate `evidence_trial_ids` during MDL compression and raw-to-pattern promotion. **Legacy quarantine fallback fail-closed behavior landed 2026-06-19** in `15f3ec8`: `KnowledgeDistiller` and `StructuralLab` now raise if a caller supplies a journal or explicit excluded-trial set but the injected store lacks `strategy_entries_for_distillation()` or `strategy_rows_for_compression()`, so journal-aware promotion cannot silently fall back to raw SQL. **Journal-keyed frontier strategy projection landed 2026-06-19** in `887de60`: AutoPilot no longer writes B1 frontier strategy rows before `journal.record()`; boxes.text: **W1 — ratchet + double-check hotfixes** (impl 0.1+0.2, ~1 day): `safety_gate.py` `update_baseline` now requires same-tier frontier reproduction evidence (min 3) and promotes the representative median; `gate.check()` caches verdicts per `EvalResult` so repeated calls do not double-count MAD/consecutive-failure state. **W4 — instrument repair** (impl 2.0, 2–3 days): `expected==''` now scores only for expected-free scorers (`code_execution`, `programmatic`) and sampled empty-expected text-scorer rows are consciously replaced from the same suite; pandas is installed in the uv dev env; VL trace root cause was dual plumbing (image requests could enter learned text routing + OCR inherited a missing/stale `llama-mtmd-cli` path). Repairs landed in `acd0f7e`, `8446d86`, and `41b0ce8`: NFKD fold, T0 `sentinel_<suite>` namespacing, Seeder per-question seen-state persistence, image requests bypass learned text routing, OCR MTMD fallback/subprocess library path fix. **EXL3-R1 — Establish the architecture boundary.** Existing NVIDIA and RDNA kernels supply algorithms, layouts, and failure cases, but do not provide MI210 support or predict gfx90a performance. ✅ 2026-09-25
**EXL3-R2 — Establish the MI210 target.** Compile for exact `gfx90a`, wave64, and the chosen CDNA2 MFMA forms; `gfx9-generic` is insufficient. ✅ 2026-09-25
**EXL3-R3 — Establish separate decode and prefill regimes.** Decode starts with wave64 GEMV; prefill and wider batches get a separate MFMA path. ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-R4 — Establish the CPU starting point.** Reuse upstream `mul1` scheduling, ISA, and swizzle patterns; begin MCG from an independent scalar oracle because no optimized MCG CPU path or transferable `mul1` fusion has been established. ✅ 2026-09-25
**EXL3-R5 — Establish the dispatch uncertainty.** Preserve unified runtime-K and grouped K-specialized paths until local EPYC and MI210 measurements select per-regime defaults. ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-R6 — Establish the quality comparison boundary.** W4A16 is an alternative deployment family, but codec claims require matched teacher, architecture, expert plan, evaluation panel, and storage budget. ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-R7 — Freeze the native-packed execution contract.** The strongest transferable implementation pattern is per-logical-matrix metadata plus a plan/bind/run lifecycle over native packed tensors, caller-owned persistent scratch, fixed capacities, and fail-closed codebook/device checks. The CUDA implementations do not transfer to gfx90a; the contracts do. (`intake-1756#00`, `intake-1756#01`, `intake-1757#00`, `intake-1757#01`, `intake-1757#02`) ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-R8 — Freeze the first real MCG fixture and oracle boundary.** Uniform K4/MCG is the first real fixture. The independent project oracle must cover packed windows and lane placement; generation identity and a quality receipt do not substitute for raw reconstruction parity. Source-available Brandon code remains evidence-only unless license review authorizes reuse. (`intake-1756#02`, `intake-1758#00`, `intake-1758#02`, `intake-1758#03`) ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-R9 — Freeze the throughput attribution boundary.** Published NVIDIA rates combine target quantization, speculative acceptance, scheduler behavior, graph capture, attention/KV precision, and recurrent-state handling. CPU/MI210 qualification must measure operator and full-stack envelopes separately. (`intake-1563#record`, `intake-1564#record`, `intake-1754#record`, `intake-1779#record`) ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-R10 — Freeze the full-stack correctness boundary.** Exactness is proposition-specific: packed reconstruction, operator output, recurrent state, verifier acceptance, and complete autoregressive token equality require separate oracles and fail-capable controls. (`intake-1760#00`, `intake-1760#01`, `intake-1760#02`, `intake-1763#00`, `intake-1763#01`, `intake-1765#record`, `intake-1767#record`) ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-R11 — Close broad literature expansion.** No reviewed source supplies CPU/gfx90a EXL3 throughput or invalidates the custom-kernel path. Reopen research only for actual CPU/gfx90a EXL3 code, a changed ABI/reconstruction rule, evidence invalidating the correctness path, or matched raw evidence that changes a gate. ✅ 2026-09-25

**EXL3-GRAPH-1 — PROPOSED: support caller-owned outer HIP capture on the standalone unified EXL3 path.** Recover the device-resident metadata/replay application omitted when safeguards and overhead attribution were filed. Add bounded device-resident route/count/order inputs through the existing plan/bind arena, keeping eager execution and fail-closed capacity/identity checks. Specify the capture envelope; qualify changed routing and token lengths within it against the existing full-output oracle. Missing/stale metadata, overflow and unsupported fallback must refuse before output writes. Reuse the live EXL3 verifier/measurement writer and strict projection, binding exact propositions, fixture/read-set/producer identities and all failures. After the existing device correctness gates pass, compare eager and replay latency on identical frozen fixtures with interleaved repetitions, a complete denominator and a predeclared overhead disposition. No claimed speedup, parked 27B integration reopening, frozen-kernel edit or production change; GPU execution requires the owning session's coordinated claim/window. This is a filed implementation proposal, not execution authorization. [Review](../../docs/reviews/research-intake-practical-applications-20261004.md); record discussion: intake-1569#record.

**EXL3-1 — Freeze the backend-neutral artifact, metadata, oracle, and evidence contract.** ✅ 2026-09-26. Define a content-addressed canonical EXL3 manifest with tensor role/shape/order, K or `rate_x2`, codebook, trellis packing, Hadamard geometry, `suh`/`svh`, scaling, padding, and source revision. Reject unknown or conflicting metadata before allocation. Implement independent portable `mul1` and MCG reconstruction plus GEMV/GEMM references. Create project-owned K1–K8 synthetic vectors and mandatory revision-pinned real-weight `mul1` and MCG fixtures containing packed states, reconstructed tiles, transforms, and full operator outputs. Backend repacks must bind the canonical input digest. Before the first correctness, performance, or quality run, land the `VB-EXL3-CPU-GFX90A` writer and strict projection for `epyc.exl3.measurement.v1` and `epyc.exl3.verifier.v1`; this task cannot close before both are live. Measurement rows use the locator run × arm × backend × operator × shape × metric and carry producer/schema identity, producer hash, run/row IDs, self-hash, one metric with units and direction, exact category, protocol ID (empty when ineligible), repetitions and basis, date, attestation path/digest, raw vector, comparator/arm identity, experimental authority, and model/artifact/source/binary/library/toolchain/hardware/residency identities. Verifier rows use run × fixture × backend/path × proposition and additionally bind checker identity/hash, fixture and read-set digests, the exact `decided_proposition`, and verdict.

**EXL3-2 — Implement and qualify the EPYC primitives.** ✅ 2026-09-26. Land scalar dense and indexed-expert operators first, then AVX-512BW/VNNI/VBMI `mul1` GEMV and an independently vectorized MCG path. Cover native and band-contiguous layouts, supported ISA tiers, K1–K8, one through four rows, tails, padding, guard-filled outputs, and real fixtures that cannot silently skip. Compare grouped-by-K dispatch outside the hot loop with per-expert runtime K. Start prefill with canonical reconstruction into the project GEMM provider; optimize a many-row path only after profiling.

**EXL3-3 — Build the native gfx90a reconstruction oracle and wave64 decode GEMV.** Freeze the ROCm 6.2 build contract and record compiler, exact target ID, code-object version, XNACK/SRAMECC mode, emitted object hash, and disassembly. Validate wave64 lane maps and procedural integer state operations, then implement K3/K4 `mul1` and MCG first with FP32 accumulation and stable reduction. Cover dense and expert tensors, boundaries, bias, padded and unpadded projections, poisoned padding, and teardown without residue. The first architecture milestone is matching full operator outputs against EXL3-1 and EXL3-2 on both real fixtures.

**EXL3-3a — decide the GEMV oracle envelope: reference-order accumulation vs a declared tolerance.** (filed 2026-10-03 from the first device run) Either make the device GEMV reduce in the canonical oracle's order (then demand exact equality), or have the oracle emit a reference-order-independent bound (e.g. Σ|w·x|·K·ε_fp32 per output) and declare it in the G1/G3 envelope. Re-run the three real fixtures; G3 closes only on a pass under the declared envelope, decided before the re-run.

**EXL3-3b — the claimed-run teardown guard turns a passing binary into rc 2.** (filed 2026-10-03) `scripts/kernel_rnd/exl3_gfx90a/claimed_run.py` takes two teardown samples 20 ms apart and sets `code = code or 2` if the exited PID is still listed in KFD. On the synthetic run the first sample still listed PID 1670889 after the process was reaped (`pid_alive` false) and the second was empty — a KFD bookkeeping lag, not residue. Poll until the PID leaves KFD or a bounded timeout (fail only on the timeout), keep the samples in `residency.json`, add a test, then re-run the synthetic suite.

**EXL3-4 — Build the native gfx90a MFMA prefill path after EXL3-3 correctness.** Create a standalone FP16-input/FP32-accumulating 16×16×16 lane-map harness, decode packed trellis tiles into register or LDS fragments, apply the required transforms, and fuse them with MFMA. Compare folded and unfolded reconstruction against the same reference and record scratch, LDS, occupancy, HBM, launch, and latency data. Keep the GEMV and MFMA dispatch surfaces separate.

**EXL3-5 — Make mixed-K MoE dispatch total and correct.** Carry device-visible half-bit K/rate and codebook metadata, projection pointer tables, and explicit local/global expert domains. Implement unified runtime-K and grouped K-specialized policies plus named batched, small-row, and single-expert fallbacks. Centralize eligibility in one capability truth table. Count/sort arrays may use sentinel E; local compute/gather tables have exactly E entries. Preserve routing-k order, explicit top-k bounds, deterministic fixed-order FP32 gather, and a separately labeled atomic mode. Exercise BC present/absent, extension present/absent, batch and routed-row thresholds, buckets below four experts, all-local/all-nonlocal/mixed slices, and every fallback. Require full operator-output or logit comparisons; token equality is insufficient.

**EXL3-X0 — Bytes-elasticity and equal-bytes quality pre-gate on the production 27B (operator-approved 2026-10-03, ahead of EXL3-6).** In one exclusive :8083 window, run unsloth UD-Q4_K_M against the incumbent Q8_0 (same publisher, byte-identical) through the DFlash2-np4 serving recipe and the production shape, 3 launches per arm, ABA. Add KLD of Q4_K_M against Q8_0 on the MI210. Decision rule, fixed in advance: if Q4_K_M is under +10% serving speed, EXL3 has no speed case on the 27B; park EXL3-6/7 for it and settle VRAM with GGUF. If it is at or above +10%, fund a performance-grade wave64 kernel (EXL3-P) with a 5-agent-day kill. EXL3-3/4/5 device correctness piggybacks on the same window. turboderp `Qwen3.8-27B-exl3` 4.00bpw is on disk for real-tensor correctness and the later equal-bytes comparison. Plan: `/mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/x0-27b-quants/PLAN.md`. ROI review: [`docs/reviews/exl3-roi-20261003.md`](../../docs/reviews/exl3-roi-20261003.md).

**EXL3-X0b — settle the 27B's GGUF quant in the post-MI210-#2 topology.** (filed 2026-10-03) **Trigger-gated (operator 2026-10-03): no quant switch without a significant speedup — reopen only if AutoKernel unlocks big low-quant gains (EXL3-LB1a).** Was: operator decision, waiting on the second MI210's arrival: keep Q8_0, or take UD-Q4_K_M (mean KLD 0.0076, same-top-p 96.1%, +11.36 GiB free at the production shape, no decode gain at np1). Inputs: the X0 report above. Not an EXL3 task; it lands as a stack change when the topology is redrawn.

**EXL3-X0c — re-run the X0 production-shape comparison (Q8_0 vs UD-Q4_K_M) on the seed #1 build, if EXL3-LB1b confirms.** (filed 2026-10-04) 3 launches per arm, ABA, temp0 and default sampling, ~2k and ~50k, plus a Q8_0-on-seed-#1 arm (the route also touches Q6_K, so Q8_0's own number must be re-measured on the same binary). KLD from X0 carries over (same files). Output: the decision package for EXL3-X0b — speed gain, KLD 0.0076, +11.36 GiB VRAM — for the operator.

**EXL3-LB1 — Low-bit GPU decode kernels as an AutoKernel GPU target (operator discussion 2026-10-03; sequenced after X0 + KLD, preferably on MI210 #2).** Rationale: MI210 has about 14 vector ops per HBM byte against about 38 on an RTX 3090 (spec-sheet arithmetic, not measured), so low-bit decode should hit an instruction/occupancy wall well before the bandwidth roofline; llama.cpp HIP Q4_K decode sits at 35.1% of roofline against Q8_0 50.2% ([`mi210-q8-dequant-gemv-roofline.md`](mi210-q8-dequant-gemv-roofline.md), quant ladder). This is the same question EXL3-P would answer with a new format, asked of the GGUF formats we already serve.

Open only for a model or shape where a bytes-elasticity pre-gate shows one.* Add the canonical loader, one linear/indexed-expert operation, scalar fallback, CPU backend, and HIP backend without editing frozen v10. files.title: findings-05c — MI210 gfx90a Speed Campaign: Lever × Model-Category Isolation

boxes.text: **N-gram / prompt-lookup on GPU** (L12) — **SUPERSEDED, do not run** ✅ 2026-08-12 (`mainB`).

**MTP on fp16/bf16** (L8) ✅ 2026-07-06 — MTP **+60.2%** on F16 (Qwen3.6-27B, Q8→F16 dequant proxy, α 66.9%≈Q8, mean-accept 3.00/3) vs Q8's +15.6% → BW-bound hypothesis CONFIRMED (F16 2 bytes/param → each accepted draft avoids a fatter weight read). **Caveat:** F16 abs 31.0 t/s MTP stays BELOW Q8 40.4 (MTP+MMQ) — F16 is a precision choice, not a throughput one; MTP just makes it far more affordable. TRUE-fp16 download pending to confirm real α + measure quality headroom (proxy α is Q8-valued).

**KV-quant single-stream long-ctx** (L14) — dense-Q8 **and** GDN full-global layers at 64k single-stream ✅ 2026-08-14 (frozen v9 `0db32c06e`/`10125`, observation-grade): **DEAD — the "alive" hypothesis is FALSIFIED.** At 64k single-stream, `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` **hurts** decode on both arms: 35B-A3B GDN hybrid **75.8 → 63.1 t/s (−16.7%)**, dense 27B **21.7 → 20.2 t/s (−6.9%)**. The dequant cast cost exceeds the KV bandwidth saving even on the dense 27B (all-full-global KV, where the KV read most rivals weight bytes). Matches the CPU precedent ("dequant cast COSTS throughput"). Closes the [U]/[H] "alive" cell with data; KV-quant stays a max-context/VRAM characterization only, not a speed lever. Evidence: `/tmp/opencode/l14_kv_{f16,q8_0}.log`, `/tmp/opencode/l14_d27_{f16,q8_0}.log`.

**FA-decode A/B on the MoE frontdoor** (L22) ✅ 2026-07-06 — MEASURED (35B-A3B-Q8): −fa0 single-stream (99.64>94.68, +5.2%) / −fa1 aggregate B≥16 (342.3>333.0 @B32, +2.8%). MoE crossover holds but MARGINAL (GDN suppresses the attention fraction FA targets; gemma-26B pure-MoE was +16%). Coherence PASS.

**Tree-draft GPU re-test** (L11) ✅ 2026-07-06 — DySpec Phase 1a ported + validated on the v7-candidate (engine bit-identical to linear draft) then **SHELVED**: external-drafter tree is DOMINATED by embedded MTP on every stack target (qwen-27B MTP 41.9 vs tree ~18 < plain 31), and GLM-5.2 also ships an MTP head → no MTP-less niche remains. Native-GLM-MTP forward-graph port is the better future lever (gated on GLM-5.2 runnability). See [tree-draft-forward-port-plan.md](tree-draft-forward-port-plan.md).
**EAGLE-3 on pure-dense** (L10) — needs a trained head + relax `target_layer_ids_n==3`; also gemma-MoE untested.
**Corpus-static n-gram (−lcs)** (L13) — build chunk-and-merge bigram cache from a few-GB code slice, vocab-locked; then A/B.
**Sub-4-bit capacity/throughput** (L15) — only after a CDNA2 sub-4-bit dequant kernel exists; PPL/eval-parity gate.
**GPU-draft / CPU-target spec** (L18) — for overflow-to-CPU MoE (122B, GLM-5.2 IQ2) and CPU-target GDN roles.
**quantize_q8_1 requant kill** (L2) — low effort, do early.

**Fused dequant-in-GEMV** (L3) ✅ 2026-07-14 — RESOLVED NON-TASK (a8afd338 reconciliation): Q8_0 GEMV is already int8-native (`vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1` = dp4a + one fp scale/32-block), no per-element dequant to hide; the 47→62% gap is BW/occupancy, not dequant-compute.

**Async weight prefetch / LDS double-buffer** (L4) ✅ 2026-07-14 — MEASURED + landed: nwarps 2→4 +4.6% (`5dc116130`), `raw.buffer.load.lds` LDS double-buffer +3.3% (`7c28056b7`, MemUnitStalled −62%). +3.3% is the CDNA2 LDS-prefetch ceiling; fused-FFN extension FALSIFIED.
**Weight swizzle / SoA Q8_0 repack** (L6) — gate on `TCC_EA_RDREQ_32B`; do jointly with L3.

**Persistent / megakernel decode** (L5) ✅ 2026-07-14 — RESOLVED NEGATIVE (2026-07-04 Pass-2): NOT worth building. HIP graphs (kill ALL host-launch) buy only +5.9%; decode is memory-latency-bound at ~50% roofline, so the 62→100% gap is the batch-1 MLP floor, not a launch bubble. Single-stream dense-Q8 CLOSED.
**MFMA compute-bound kernels** (L7) — prefill / DiT denoise / ViT encoder / high-batch expert GEMM; profile-gated (high VALUBusy + low MfmaUtil).

**GDN occupancy + recurrent-state traffic/layout** (L20) ✅ 2026-07-14 — bf16-state BUILT + GO (`496e2f098`): +21.5%@B32 (drift+isolation PASS), deployed on frontdoor + architect. Occupancy sub-lever was NO-GO; bf16-state is the win.
**Q4_K dequant efficiency** (L21) — ~+43% → ~47 t/s single-stream, quality-gated.
**mmid MoE dispatch threshold** (L1-MoE) — the deferred production-relevant MoE analog; most valuable at 256-expert sparsity.
**Diffusion serving path + all DiT levers** (§3.5) — no path exists yet.
**Auxiliary baselines (BGE encode, VL prefill)** (§3.6) — no aux model ever benchmarked; the entire Aux column is currently deductive.

**Dense-Q4_K / K-quant** — the registry **default** quant (Q4_K 291 hits), a distinct 33%-roofline dequant regime where L1 barely applies (+5.8% vs +17–32% Q8). Treated as a lever, is really a category.
**Pure-MoE vs GDN-hybrid-MoE split** inside "MoE-on-GPU-decode" — the campaign's own sharpest distinction (spec-dec viable + 5.9–8.6x scaling for pure-MoE vs net-negative + 3.4x for GDN-hybrid-MoE).
**Sub-4-bit / IQ codebook quant** — architecturally different dequant kernel from K-quant block dequant; the bytes/token axis deciding 64 GB fit.
**MLA-attention MoE** (GLM-4.7-Flash frontdoor candidate, deepseek2) — latent-compressed KV **flips the L14 KV-quant math**; spec-dec-forbidden.

**Mamba2-hybrid** (Nemotron-Cascade-2 frontdoor candidate) — float32 SSM state (~2× traffic), 88% recurrent; must **not** inherit delta-net GDN verdicts (`--mamba-ssm-dtype` is its own recurrent-traffic knob).
**Lightning / linear-attention hybrid** (Ring, bailingmoe_linear) — a third distinct linear kernel, neither delta-net nor Mamba2.
**VL split** (ViT vision-**encoder** prefill = compute-bound MFMA target; VL decoder = full MoE/dense decode; spec-dec mmproj-forbidden) — currently hidden inside "Auxiliary(vision)."

**VL vision-encoder prefill baseline — the unrun half of A3.** 2026-08-12 ran the BGE encode half only (13 GPU points, `artifacts/gpu-aux-baselines/a3_bge_mi210_20260812.jsonl`, commit `182f30b6`): bge-m3 Q8_0 and f16 land within noise at every sequence point, so **the quant lever is inert on encode** and buys memory, not speed. The VL prefill half was never run and is the compute-bound MFMA regime where L16's bf16-vs-Q8 crossover is actually testable — the row's own ⚙︎corrected note says VL prefill, not the decode tail, is the correct auxiliary analog. Needs a GPU window; nothing blocks it.
**Ultra-sparse MoE** (MiniMax-M2, 256-of-8) — where expert-gather/scatter and the mmid dispatch behave very differently than at A3B/A4B.
**ASR / speech encoder-decoder** (Whisper large-v3-turbo) — conv frontend + bidirectional encoder + cross-attention decoder fits none of the 6 buckets.

The DATA gate is now satisfied by 100 trusted reviewed triage labels plus initial F2 gold tuples; gfx90a TRAINING-VIABILITY is still [unverified] — a LoRA/GRPO/SFT smoke on a small model via TRL/verl-ROCm must pass before any of (a)–(c) is scoped. NOTE: gradient-based QLoRA (below) is what rides the training-viability gate; a gradient-FREE Evolution-Strategies path (intake-564/563, forward-pass-only) would sidestep it entirely and is tracked in learned-routing-controller.md)**: (a) planner-distill — QLoRA a Qwen3.5-9B-class base on W2's SFT set, acceptance: shadow-draft mode with ≥80% cloud-critic approval over 100 trials before any binding use; (b) drafters per the α measurement (FastDraft path, already gated in backlog); (c) judge/rubric model for EV-9 (unblocks rubric-scored suites in F1-W3) — acceptance: each fine-tune gets a MEASUREMENT.md protocol entry before its first reported number.

**Build `bitsandbytes` from source for gfx90a / ROCm 6.2** ✅ 2026-08-12 — built at tag `0.50.0` with `cmake -DCOMPUTE_BACKEND=hip -DBNB_ROCM_ARCH=gfx90a`, source at `/mnt/raid0/llm/tools/bitsandbytes-src`, installed into the `geak-v1-rocm62-py312` venv. **Verified with a real NF4 QLoRA run, not an import**: 168 `Linear4bit` modules materialised, 451.3 MB footprint (vs ~1 GB bf16), loss `1.1122 → 0.4062` (**63.5%** drop) over 60 steps, 3,102 MB peak VRAM. **4-bit QLoRA is now available on gfx90a.** The PyPI wheel remains broken here — it ships only a ROCm 6.4 code object and dies with `no kernel image is available for execution on the device`; anyone reinstalling from PyPI silently loses this.

**A GRPO run that demonstrates LEARNING, not just execution.** The 2026-08-12 smoke proved the loop runs; it proved nothing about optimisation, because `clipped_ratio: 1` meant every completion hit the token cap and the length reward could not be moved. Needs: a reward the policy can actually change, `max_completion_length` above the natural completion length so terminations are real, and a **pre-registered** pass rule (e.g. final-quintile mean reward above first-quintile by a stated margin, fixed before the run). Until that exists, no GRPO quality claim is licensed.
**Confirm bf16 LoRA on a 9B-class base fits the MI210 before spending that build.** ✅ 2026-09-15 —
Repeat the W3(a) fit check on the real Qwen3.5-9B once its HF weights are local (~19 GB download, operator

_(superseded estimate, kept for the record)_ **Confirm bf16 LoRA on a 9B-class base fits the MI210 before spending that build.** Arithmetic says ~22–25 GB against 64 GB, which would retire the 4-bit requirement for W3(a) entirely. One load + a few steps settles it. Do this task *first* — it may delete the one above.

**Environment split is deliberate — do not "consolidate" it.** Two training venvs exist on purpose, each internally consistent: `geak-v1-rocm62-py312` (torch `2.5.1+rocm6.2`, system ROCm 6.2) carries **SFT + 4-bit QLoRA**, both verified; the ROCm 6.3 venv carries **GRPO only**. **The reason is a mixed-runtime hazard, the ROCm analogue of the three-ggml-generations rule in CLAUDE.md:** the source-built `libbitsandbytes_rocm62.so` has **zero torch linkage** and resolves `libhipblas`/`libhipblaslt`/`librocblas`/`librocsolver` from **system `/opt/rocm` 6.2**, while a `+rocm6.3` torch wheel bundles its **own** ROCm 6.3 copies — loading both puts two ROCm runtimes in one address space. Compounding it, `bitsandbytes/cextension.py` selects its library by **runtime-detected ROCm version**, so under a 6.3 torch it looks for `libbitsandbytes_rocm63.so`, which does not exist (the built file is `_rocm62`); `BNB_ROCM_VERSION=62` would force it, but that deliberately pairs a 6.2-linked kernel with a 6.3 runtime and would need a numerical check, not just a successful load. Rebuilding bnb against 6.3 is not possible here — `/opt/rocm` **is** 6.2. Hence: never run bitsandbytes in the 6.3 venv.

**GRPO end-to-end smoke on gfx90a** ✅ 2026-08-12 — **mechanical viability only; learning is NOT demonstrated and is not claimed.** 8 GRPO steps completed at 11.3 samples/s, 3,276 MB peak VRAM, GPU residency sampled during the run, `grad_norm` finite throughout (3.3–6.1). The full RL loop executes: generation → reward → advantage → policy update through a LoRA adapter. **What it does not show:** reward went `-5.667 → -4.854` while bouncing (`-4.021`, `-5.583`, `-3.25`) — that is noise. `completions/clipped_ratio: 1` and `mean_terminated_length: 0` mean every completion hit the 16-token cap and none terminated naturally, so the length reward was unoptimizable by construction. A learning claim needs a reward the policy can actually move and a pre-registered rule; this smoke had neither, by design.

boxes.text: **GC-0 — Evidence hygiene / runner contract**: reviewer-facing GLM long-output or typed-decision probes must consume only instrumented GLM runs with streaming progress, retained trace logs/server-log timing extraction, and a minimum completion-token floor. `/metrics` samples are acceptable when available, but are not the primary progress channel for a long busy GLM request. **GC-0a — Current-source 32K needle/coherence gate executed**: default reasoning and `--reasoning off --reasoning-budget 0` both completed full prompt ingest plus 64-token decode, then llama-server returned HTTP 500 because generated output did not match `peg-native`; hidden code `GLM52-NEEDLE-7F3A` was absent.
